title: Would you consider a versatile actor or an actor with an irreplaceable niche as the greatest?

commenti.body:
What do you mean by “most irreplaceable in his own genre”? Do you mean someone like John Wayne? He’s someone that is iconic in his genre but who’s acting abilities are almost nonexistent. So I don’t know why this would be the defining thing in terms of who is the greatest actor. 

Versatility is pretty overrated as well. The amount of people who can do 20 different characters in a superficial way is bigger than the amount of people who can do a few characters in a genius way. Versatility gets praised because the acting skill is more visible. 

I would say that it should be depth, insight and the ability to express these things which are the defining characteristics of a great actor. People will praise an actor because they “believed” them in the role but I think it needs to go further than that. The actor needs to make you feel like your understanding of not just the character but also the situations they’re in is greater after watching their performance. Great acting and great art in general is about pulling out details that most people didn’t realize were there.

I am in the camp of versatility.  Your trade is being an actor, that is what you are paid for.  You should be able to play any role within your physical capabilities.  If you think of who are considered the greatest actors, they will all be versatile.

I would also not really understand what is meant with "irreplaceable in their genre".  The only ones I could then think of is action heroes like Schwarzenegger, Stallone and their action hero successors like currently Johnson is.
I don't think versatility is a required thing for great actors. Sure it's impressive but why does what an actor can or can't do outside of the movie your watching affect that performance

a versatile actor still has to be consistent. someone who has mastered 1 character and uses variations of that character in their work is bound to be relatively consistent. conversely, an actor who has taken on many characters is impressively malleable, but are they able to put the same quality in their work?

i'd say the actor with the best performance is the best actor. it's also impossible to measure the quality of a performance without also knowing the actor and knowing who they really are. is the character they are playing different from who they are? how much has the actor convinced you to be true about their performance?

Whichever option describes Daniel Day-Lewis most accurately.

Jokes aside, I don't think either versatility or nailing down a niche should be a consideration for deciding if someone is a great actor or not. As long as an actor consistently justifies their performance in the roles they choose.

I do value versatility. There are people like Day-Lewis, Brando, Binoche, Swinton who are very versatile and can be legitimately be claimed as some of the best actors ever.

But then, if someone made a claim for someone like Jean-Pierre Leaud or Lee Kang-Sheng (who has played not more than a total of 3 or 4 characters over his entire career), I would understand that too.

>If you think of who are considered the greatest actors, they will all be versatile.

Except... for most people, that isn't actually true.

Al Pacino and Robert De Niro tend to not exactly blend in to a role.

My favorite actor is Jack Nicholson.

I love Brad Pitt, actually, and also Nicolas Cage.  Not the greatest comedians.

Even someone like Denzel Washington... I mean, dude is basically always the same character.

I could go on and on...

The reality is most stars have a very persistent persona.  And it tends to be the stars we gravitate towards.

Now, I am personally okay with someone saying they value versatility.  And there are certainly plenty of actors that take very different roles or even famously alter their physical appearance (even a Christian Bale that seems to make it a requirement)... but I disagree that most people actually value versatility very highly.

I'd even argue versatility tends to be a detriment to becoming the kind of recognizable star that most people are going to even want to think about all.

Having said all that:  Tilda Swinton is greatest actor alive today and I'll fight anyone that says otherwise!
